questions.question: Economic growth is properly measured as:
options: The increase in REAL GDP — inflation stripped out — and per capita, since a faster-growing population means shrinking shares
The number of new companies registered

questions.question: On the Lorenz curve, deeper sag below the diagonal means:
options: WORSE inequality — the poorest have collected a smaller share of total income at each point in the line-up

questions.question: South Africa's Gini coefficient of around 0,65 signifies:
options: Inequality among the HIGHEST ever recorded — the anchor fact of every redistribution essay

questions.question: "Redistribution needs growth, and growth needs redistribution" means:
options: Growth should wait for equality first
Grants and services need a growing tax base to fund them, while a widening of participation feeds growth — the pot must grow WHILE the shares move

questions.question: The Human Development Index combines:
options: LIFE EXPECTANCY, EDUCATION and INCOME per person — so a healthier, better-schooled country can outrank a richer one

questions.question: "Growth without development" describes:
options: GDP rising while health, education and opportunity STAGNATE — the distinction the topic is built on

questions.question: South Africa's succession of development plans runs:
options: RDP for basic needs, GEAR for stability, AsgiSA for constraints, NDP as the current framework

questions.question: Indigenous knowledge systems matter for development because they:
options: Cut costs, fit local conditions and carry OWNERSHIP that imported blueprints lack — development done WITH people compounds

questions.question: The two families of globalisation's causes are:
options: TECHNOLOGY making it possible — containers, cables, computing — and POLICY making it permitted — tariff cuts, freed finance, reopened economies

questions.question: The 2008 crisis reaching South African factories within a year demonstrates:
options: CONTAGION — in one interconnected system, a foreign financial collapse destroys jobs far from its origin

questions.question: The terms-of-trade treadmill traps Southern economies because:
options: They export too little raw material
Raw export prices SWING and SAG over time against the manufactured goods they import — selling raw and buying made buys less each year
Northern countries buy nothing from the South

questions.question: The balanced verdict on globalisation is that it:
options: GROWS the world's total while MOVING the shares — so policy must capture gains and cushion losses

questions.question: A negative externality makes the market fail because the outside cost is:
options: Priced at ZERO by the market — so the product is too cheap and society gets TOO MUCH of it

questions.question: "What belongs to everyone is cared for by no one" explains:
options: The overuse of COMMONS — each user takes one more unit because the loss is shared while the gain is private

questions.question: South Africa's carbon tax is an example of:
options: A MARKET INSTRUMENT — putting the missing price on pollution so the polluter pays the social cost

questions.question: Sustainability means:
options: Using no natural resources at all
Meeting present needs WITHOUT compromising future generations — living off nature's interest without eating the capital

subtopics.title: The Pot and the Queue of One Hundred

questions.question: "A pot two percent bigger feeding a family two percent larger has grown nobody's plate" teaches that:
options: Growth must be measured REAL and PER CAPITA before celebrating — our country's last decade in one sentence

questions.question: Walking past sixty people in the queue and counting barely a tenth of the food describes:
options: The LORENZ CURVE done on foot — the deep sag of South African inequality

questions.question: The "handle" on the grants spoon is that grants:
options: Need a GROWING pot to fund them — relief now depends on a tax base that keeps expanding

subtopics.title: Taller or Better — and the One-World Shop

questions.question: "Taller" against "better" distinguishes:
options: GROWTH — the pot getting bigger — from DEVELOPMENT — the whole report card of health, schooling and freedom

questions.question: "A modern skyline visible from a subsistence village" is the sign called:
options: DUALISM — two economies in one view, one of the six signs of a developing country

questions.question: The honest verdict on South Africa's development plans is:
options: Excellent DIAGNOSIS, thin DELIVERY — the gap between paper and ground is the recurring finding

questions.question: "The way up is to finish what we dig and grow" argues that South Africa should:
options: Move up the value chain — roasting, branding, manufacturing — so the profitable finishing happens on this side of the map, as AfCFTA intends

subtopics.title: The Smoke, the River and the Seed Mealies

questions.question: The bricks are priced too cheap because:
options: The smoke costs the factory NOTHING — the village's costs never reach the books, so the world orders too many bricks

questions.question: "Give the river a guardian" summarises which fixes?
options: Rules with teeth, community ownership, or capped tradeable permits — each makes the river's limits appear in everyone's arithmetic

questions.question: "Eating the seed mealies" stands for:
options: Consuming the CAPITAL that does the regrowing — fish faster than breeding, water faster than rain, a stable climate burned away

questions.question: South Africa's pantry is exposed because the country is:
options: Water-scarce and warming fast, swinging between drought and flood, and powered mostly by coal while the world starts taxing carbon at its borders
